title: Turkish Cheese Map: Kars Gravyer, Ezine, Van Otlu & İzmir Tulum
seoTitle: Turkish Cheese Map: Kars Gravyer, Ezine, Van Otlu & Tulum
metaDescription: Turkish cheese guide to Kars gravyer, Ezine, Van otlu and İzmir tulum, where to buy in Istanbul, customs rules for flying home, and wine pairings.
quickAnswer: Türkiye produces nearly 200 regional cheeses, anchored by four benchmark styles: nutty highland Kars gravyer, EU-PDO Ezine white cheese, wild-herb Van otlu peyniri, and sharp brined İzmir tulum. You can taste and buy all four in Istanbul's Kadıköy, Karaköy, and Spice Bazaar markets—though strict EU, UK, and US customs rules govern flying home with dairy.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Deep Culinary, Regional Food & Beverage Guides

body.text: A reliable turkish cheese guide looks far past generic supermarket feta. Anatolia's altitude swings—from Aegean olive hills to 2,200-metre eastern plateaus—support sheep, goat, and pasture-fed cow herds whose milk changes flavour with every season's wild flora.
Which regional artisan cheeses belong on a serious Turkish tasting board?

A balanced Turkish cheese board pairs four distinct textures and milk profiles: Kars gravyer (Swiss-lineage alpine cow's-milk wheel), Ezine peyniri (creamy, brined sheep-goat-cow white cheese from Çanakkale), Van otlu peyniri (sheep's-milk cheese packed with wild mountain garlic and herbs), and İzmir tulum (tangy, crumbly, brine-ripened Aegean sheep-and-goat cheese).

Each of these four carries deep regional protection. Boğatepe (Kars) Gravyer is recognised as a [Slow Food Presidium](https://www.fondazioneslowfood.com/en/slow-food-presidia/bog%CC%86atepe-gravyer/), tracing its alpine cheesemaking craft to late-19th-century Caucasus and Swiss cheesemakers who settled near Kars. Ezine Peyniri became the first Turkish cheese registered as an EU Protected Designation of Origin, as confirmed by the [Turkish Patent and Trademark Office](https://www.turkpatent.gov.tr/en/news/eu-registration-for-ezine-peyniri). Van Otlu Peyniri holds Turkish Geographical Indication No. 405 ([Türk Patent GI Registry PDF](https://ci.turkpatent.gov.tr/Files/GeographicalSigns/5c08a8d5-8481-48a9-911e-8a5a1b3186b2.pdf)), incorporating endemic eastern herbs such as sirmo (wild garlic). Finally, İzmir Tulum Peyniri earned Turkish GI registration in 2022 ([KÜRE Encyclopedia — İzmir Tulum](https://kureansiklopedi.com/en/detay/izmir-tulum-cheese-7fcf9)), prized for its firm, crumbly bite alongside ripe figs and walnuts.
Where in Istanbul (Kadıköy, Karaköy, Mısır Çarşısı) can you buy aged Kars gravyer and Van herbed cheese?

You do not need to fly to eastern Anatolia to shop well: Istanbul's Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı), Karaköy's historic delicatessens along Mumhane and Necatibey streets, and the outer market lanes beside Mısır Çarşısı (the Spice Bazaar) stock genuine aged Kars gravyer, genuine Ezine wheels, and small-batch Van herbed cheese.

Skip souvenir stalls inside tourist corridors that display unrefrigerated blocks under hot lights. Instead, head to high-turnover neighbourhood şarküteri (delicatessens) where local shoppers queue every morning. Always ask for a sliver to taste before buying, confirm whether an Ezine block is koyun (sheep), keçi (goat), or mixed milk, and check the rind of Kars gravyer for natural golden-brown ageing rather than waxy yellow paraffin. If you are also exploring Marmara dairy towns, pair your Istanbul market walk with stops in our [Bursa destination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa), famous for Mihaliç sheep's cheese.
Can you vacuum-pack Turkish cheese to fly home legally?

Most reputable Istanbul şarküteri shops will vacuum-seal (vakumlatmak) hard cheeses free of charge, keeping them fresh for 24 to 48 hours in checked luggage—but customs legality depends entirely on your destination country. Travellers returning to the European Union or Great Britain are generally prohibited from bringing dairy products from Türkiye, whereas United States travellers may bring certain hard, cured cheeses if declared.
Never rely on shopkeeper reassurance at the counter; border rules are enforced strictly to prevent animal diseases such as foot-and-mouth disease:

items: European Union (Banned): Under [European Commission Food Safety personal import rules](https://food.ec.europa.eu/animals/animal-products-movements/personal-imports_en), travellers arriving from non-EU countries—including Türkiye—are not allowed to bring meat, milk, or dairy products such as cheese in personal luggage.

Great Britain / UK (Banned): Under [GOV.UK rules on bringing food into Great Britain](https://www.gov.uk/bringing-food-into-great-britain/meat-dairy-fish-animal-products), you cannot bring cheese, milk, or dairy products from outside permitted exemptions into Great Britain for personal use.

United States (Restricted & Must Declare): Per [U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)](https://www.help.cbp.gov/s/article/Article-1277?language=en_US), solid, hard cured cheeses are generally admissible for personal use, whereas soft or liquid-brined cheeses risk refusal; [all travelers must declare food items to CBP](https://www.cbp.gov/travel/clearing-cbp/bringing-agricultural-products-united-states) upon arrival.
Pack smart where legal: Place vacuum-packed hard cheeses (like Kars gravyer or aged eski kaşar) in checked baggage, since soft cheeses can trigger cabin liquid-gel limits at airport security.

body.text: How do local cheeses pair with Turkish wines?

Anatolian cheeses evolved alongside native grape varieties, creating natural regional pairings across acidity, salinity, and weight. High-acid white wines made from Emir (Cappadocia) or Narince (Tokat) slice cleanly through creamy Ezine and garlicky Van otlu, while nutty Kars gravyer and crystalline İzmir tulum stand up to structured Öküzgözü and Boğazkere reds.

As [GoTürkiye's Turkish Wines guide](https://goturkiye.com/gastronomy/turkish-wines) highlights, tasting native grapes alongside cave-aged Divle Obruk, Kars kaşarı, and Kars gravyer is one of the easiest ways to understand Türkiye's terroir in a single sitting. Keep pairings simple: serve cheeses at cool room temperature (about 16–18°C) with toasted sourdough, roasted walnuts, and dried Aydın figs rather than overly sweet commercial jams.

faq.q: What is the difference between Kars gravyer and Kars eski kaşar?
faq.a: Kars gravyer is a large, eye-studded, Swiss-style alpine cow's-milk wheel aged for months until nutty and slightly sweet, whereas eski kaşar is a denser, sharper pasta-filata aged cheese with no large holes.

faq.q: Can I buy vacuum-packed cheese at Istanbul Airport duty-free instead?
faq.a: Duty-free shops occasionally stock packaged Turkish cheeses, but EU and UK personal-import bans on non-EU dairy apply regardless of whether the cheese was bought in a market or at the airport.

faq.q: What herbs are inside Van otlu peyniri?
faq.a: Traditional Van herbed cheese blends local sheep's milk with wild mountain greens harvested in spring, most notably sirmo (wild garlic), mendi, heliz, and wild mint.

faq.q: Why is Ezine cheese so creamy compared to standard white cheese?
faq.a: Genuine Ezine cheese is made from pasture-fed sheep, goat, and cow milk from the Kaz Mountains foothills and matured in brine for at least eight months, developing a rich, buttery paste rather than a chalky crumble.

faq.q: Should Turkish cheeses be refrigerated or served at room temperature?
faq.a: Store them chilled, then remove hard and brined cheeses from the fridge 30 to 45 minutes before serving so their nutty, grassy, and herbal aromas open fully.

faq.q: Which Istanbul wine bars serve serious Turkish cheese boards?
faq.a: Boutique wine bars in Karaköy, Beyoğlu, Moda (Kadıköy), and Galata routinely pour native Anatolian grapes alongside boards featuring Kars gravyer, Divle Obruk, İzmir tulum, and aged Ezine.
